newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Low global oil stocks to cushion Iraq return.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Low global oil stocks to cushion Iraq return.

text.p: Renewed Iraqi oil exports may be set to hit world oil markets soon but lean global oil stocks should prevent crude prices going into an immediate tailspin, analysts and traders said on Friday.
Rapid demand increases fired by strong economic growth, oilfield supply hiccups and a two-month interruption to Iraqi sales have all helped keep the lid on crude inventories.

"Stocks should be building heading through the summer quarter but evidence of serious stockbuilding for the month of July might not be easy to find," said consultant Roy Mason in his monthly Oil Movements report.
"For the second month running it looks as though independent evidence on the state of the global oil economy could err towards the bullish," said Mason.
London September futures for bellwether North Sea Brent blend closed almost unchanged on Friday at $18.95 a barrel.
Prices have recorded a robust recovery from the year's low of $17.32 in early June after a slump from just under $25 a barrel in six months.

Mehdi Varzi at research house Kleinwort Benson said he had reduced his estimate for the global build in oil stocks during the second quarter by 700,000 barrels a day (bpd) to 1.5 million. His forecast for the third quarter had been cut by 200,000 bpd to 1.6 million
"Inventories have grown at a much slower rate so far this year than originally feared," said Varzi.
"If you look at the stockbuild during the period of Iraq's absence and compare it with what was expected you have a totally different fundamental picture," a European oil trader said.
Kleinwort Benson also revised higher its estimate for world demand this year, by 200,000 bpd to 74 million, up 2.6 percent from 72.1 million in 1996.
Oil in transit at sea, one of the leading indicators for oil markets, was on the rise by the end of July. But Oil Movements, which tracks tankers, said the increase was from a low base.
"Seaborne oil is certainly on an upward path...What is still not clear is the size of the prospective stockbuild," the report said.
Heavy tanker chartering in recent days for key Atlantic basin markets, which tend to lead prices for the rest of the world, could spell added pressure for crude markets, it added.

Iraq's two month absence from world oil markets, awaiting a new aid distribution plan under its oil-for-food exchange with the United Nations, has shorn some 700,000 barrels a day (bpd) from world supply.
Delayed starts to new North Sea fields and a guerrilla attack on Colombia's crude export pipeline has reduced supplies elsewhere.

Traders say Iraq looks set to push as much as 1.4 million bpd to buyers in a short burst in an effort to meet the billion dollar target it is permitted in the next tranche of the agreement which expires in early September.
The United Nations says it will approve a new Iraqi aid distribution plan early next week paving the way for oil sales to restart shortly.
